Activators.none: None — the area itself triggers it

trap.label: Trap
trap.hint: ID of the trap's region on this scene. The module sets it — when placing the trap or with “Add trigger”.

pit.name: Hidden Pit
pit.text: A plank lid covered with dirt gives way under weight. A slightly sagging floor gives it away. Athletics wedges the lid shut.
pit.flavor: The floor gives way — a black pit opens beneath!

spikedPit.name: Spiked Pit
spikedPit.text: A hidden pit with sharpened stakes at the bottom. The fall hurts twice: the impact and the spikes.
spikedPit.flavor: The floor collapses — spikes glint below!

bearTrap.name: Bear Trap
bearTrap.text: Steel jaws hidden under straw or leaves. A caught creature is held in place until freed with Athletics or thieves’ tools.
bearTrap.flavor: Steel clangs underfoot — the jaws snap shut!

poisonDarts.name: Poison Darts
poisonDarts.text: A pressure plate fires darts from hidden tubes in the walls. Tiny holes in the masonry give it away; the tubes can be plugged.
poisonDarts.flavor: Darts whistle out of the walls!

arrowVolley.name: Arrow Volley
arrowVolley.text: A tripwire looses a volley from arrow slits. Everyone in the area is under fire.
arrowVolley.flavor: A click — arrows rain from the slits!

scythingBlade.name: Scything Blade
scythingBlade.text: A heavy blade swings out of a slot in the ceiling and sweeps just above the floor. The slot and scratches on the walls give the mechanism away.
scythingBlade.flavor: A huge blade whistles down from above!

fallingNet.name: Falling Net
fallingNet.text: A net hangs under the ceiling; a tripwire drops it. Anyone caught is held until they work free.
fallingNet.flavor: A heavy net drops from the ceiling!

collapsingRoof.name: Collapsing Roof
collapsingRoof.text: The supports are sawn through, and a tripwire brings the ceiling down. Cracks and fresh dust on the floor are the warning.
collapsingRoof.flavor: The ceiling groans — stones rain down!

rollingBoulder.name: Rolling Boulder
rollingBoulder.text: A pressure plate releases a stone ball that thunders through the corridor and knocks everyone down.
rollingBoulder.flavor: A rumble grows — a boulder rolls down the corridor!

fireJet.name: Fire Jet
fireJet.text: Nozzles in the walls spray flaming alchemical oil. Soot around the holes and the smell of oil give it away.
fireJet.flavor: Flame roars out of the walls!

acidSpray.name: Acid Spray
acidSpray.text: A pressurized vessel sprays acid on whoever steps on the plate. The floor around it is pitted with burns.
acidSpray.flavor: A hiss — acid sprays into your face!

poisonGas.name: Poison Gas
poisonGas.text: A plate opens valves and the room fills with caustic gas. The GM may have the door slam shut.
poisonGas.flavor: Greenish smoke creeps out of the cracks!

sleepGas.name: Sleep Gas
sleepGas.text: A sweet-smelling gas puts everyone in the area to sleep. A sleeper wakes when damaged or shaken awake.
sleepGas.flavor: The air turns sweet, eyelids grow heavy…

lightningRune.name: Lightning Rune
lightningRune.text: An invisible glyph on the floor strikes whoever steps on it with lightning. Arcana or dispel magic disables it.
lightningRune.flavor: A rune flares underfoot — lightning strikes!

frostRune.name: Frost Rune
frostRune.text: A glyph of cold covers everyone nearby in rime. The floor near it is always a little colder.
frostRune.flavor: The rune flares blue and the air rings with frost!

thunderPlate.name: Thunder Plate
thunderPlate.text: A plate carved with a glyph answers a footstep with a thunderclap that knocks everyone nearby off their feet. It can be heard far away.

witheringSigil.name: Withering Sigil
witheringSigil.text: A dark sigil drains life from everyone on it and fills them with dread. Dangerous even for seasoned heroes.
witheringSigil.flavor: Shadows reach out of the sigil and cold bites to the bone!

alarmPlate.name: Alarm Plate
alarmPlate.text: Harmless, but it rings loudly: guards and monsters learn they have guests. The GM gets a notice.
alarmPlate.flavor: Somewhere above, a bell starts ringing!

App.dragHint: Click a trap to configure it, or drag it onto the map to place it there as a hidden region.
App.empty: Nothing found. Try another search or filter.
App.sceneEmpty: No traps on this scene yet. Drag one from the library onto the map.
App.searchSelectedHint: Selected tokens roll Perception against traps within their spot range (usually 10 ft) and in line of sight.
App.triggerHint: Sets the trap off on the selected tokens, or on everyone in the area if none are selected.
App.attempt: Try to disarm with the selected token
App.confirmDelete: Remove the trap “{name}” from the scene?
App.confirmDeleteCustom: Delete your trap “{name}” from My traps?
App.revealAllHint: Reveal every trap on this scene to players
App.hideAllHint: Hide every trap on this scene from players
App.mineEmpty: Traps you configure and save show up here. Open any trap in the library or on the scene, change what you need and press “Save to My traps…” — you’ll be asked to name it.
App.mineHint: Click a trap to configure it, or drag it onto the map. Use the pencil to rename it.
App.ideaHint: Opens a form in your browser
App.addActivatorHint: Give the trap a trigger (up to three). It appears in the trap's area; move it on the map with the ✥ handle.

Hud.reveal: “{name}” is hidden from players. Click to reveal.
Hud.hide: “{name}” is visible to players. Click to hide.
Hud.noticed: “{name}” was spotted by {who}. Players can’t see it yet — click to reveal.
Hud.disarm: Disarm “{name}” with the selected token: {skill}, DC {dc}.
Hud.fire: Set off “{name}” now — on everyone in its area.
Hud.fireManual: “{name}” only fires manually. Click to set it off on everyone in its area.
Hud.move: Move “{name}” — drag. Triggers inside it move along.
Hud.addTrigger: Add a trigger to “{name}” (up to three)
Hud.rotate: Rotate “{name}” 90° — width and height swap, triggers inside turn with it

Chat.noTargets: The trap went off, but nobody is in the area.
Chat.disarmFail: {name} fails to disarm “{trap}” ({skill}: {total} vs DC {dc}). The trap didn’t go off — they can try again.
Chat.disarmTriggered: {name} slips up ({skill}: {total} vs DC {dc}) — “{trap}” goes off!
Chat.searchNoneGm: {name} searches for traps and finds nothing ({value}).
Chat.rollDamageHint: Roll damage now without waiting for the remaining saves. It’s one roll for everyone.
Chat.saveSheet: Save: {ability}, target from the character sheet
Chat.disarmFailGm: {name} fails to disarm “{trap}” ({skill}, GM’s call). It didn’t go off — try again.
Chat.disarmTriggeredGm: {name} slips up ({skill}, GM’s call) — “{trap}” goes off!
Chat.disarmAskGm: {name} tries to disarm “{trap}”: {skill}, DC {dc}. How did it go?
Chat.waitAttackGm: attack {total} vs AC — waiting for the GM
Chat.waitGm: save: {ability}, DC {dc} — waiting for the GM

Notify.gmOnly: Only the GM can do this.
Notify.noGM: A GM must be connected: traps are resolved on the GM’s side.
Notify.noticed: {name} spotted “{trap}”. Players can’t see it yet — decide in chat or with the button on the map.
Notify.otherScene: This trap is on another scene.
Notify.activatorAdded: “{name}”: trigger added. Move it on the map with the teal ✥ handle.
Notify.activatorAddedManual: “{name}”: trigger added, but the trap only fires manually — untick that in its settings.
Notify.activatorFailed: “{name}”: the trigger couldn't be placed — the trap fires from its own area. If you just updated the module, relaunch the world.
Notify.activatorMax: “{name}” already has {n} triggers — that's the limit.
Notify.noRotation: “{name}”: traps don't rotate to arbitrary angles — the ↻ button next to the trap on the map turns it 90°.
Notify.straightened: Trap Library straightened {n} rotated traps and triggers in place. To turn a trap 90°, use the ↻ button next to it on the map.

trapId.label: Based on
trapId.hint: The built-in or custom trap this one was made from.

icon.label: Icon
icon.hint: Font Awesome icon class, e.g. fa-solid fa-fire.

detectDC.label: Detect DC
detectDC.hint: Against a passive value, a secret check or a search — as set in Rules.

detectRange.label: Notice from, ft
detectRange.hint: Noticing on approach or by searching reaches this far, counted in squares like the ruler: 10 ft means one empty square in between.

disarmSkill.label: Disarmed with
disarmSkill.hint: A skill from Rules or a category (mechanism, brute force, magic).

attackBonus.label: Attack bonus
attackBonus.hint: If set, the trap attacks against AC (the AC path is in Rules; without it the GM marks hit or miss).

saveAbility.label: Save
saveAbility.hint: From the Rules list or a category (dodge, endure, resist with the mind). Empty — no save.

damage.label: Damage
damage.hint: A formula such as 2d10. Empty — no damage.

condition.label: Condition
condition.hint: A system condition, applied on a failed save or a hit. If the system has no such condition, it stays as words in the card.

sound.label: Sound
sound.hint: A built-in sound or a path to your own file.

flavor.label: Text for players
flavor.hint: Shown to players in chat when the trap goes off.

stops.label: Stops movement
stops.hint: A token that steps in stops there (pit, bear trap, net).

manual.label: Manual only
manual.hint: Doesn't fire from footsteps — only from the ▶ button on the map or Set off on the scene tab.

activators.label: Triggers
activators.hint: How many separate areas someone has to step on. With none, the trap's own area sets it off.

detectSkill.label: Noticed with
detectSkill.hint: A skill from Rules, or the Notice category — then whichever skill the GM mapped to it.

fxMode.name: Animations
fxMode.hint: Built-in animations always work. If Sequencer and JB2A are installed, their effects can be used instead.

chatMode.name: Who sees the trigger card
chatMode.hint: With “GM only”, the owners of targets still get the card when they need to roll saves.

passiveDetect.name: Notice traps on approach
passiveDetect.hint: A player character coming near a trap may notice it — how is set in Rules (passively, with a secret check, or not at all).

detectSight.name: Spot only in line of sight
detectSight.hint: Walls that block sight and closed doors stop a character from spotting a trap — on approach or by searching.

triggerBy.name: Who sets traps off
triggerBy.hint: Traps can fire on player characters only, so the GM can move monsters freely.

mapButtons.name: Trap buttons on the map
mapButtons.hint: The GM sees an eye button on every trap: one click reveals it to players or hides it. Each GM has their own setting.

detectMode.name: When a character spots a trap
detectMode.hint: What happens when a character spots a trap (on approach or by searching). You can also switch this on the On this scene tab.
detectMode.reveal: Reveal it on the map to everyone and whisper the player
detectMode.gm: Tell the GM who spotted it; reveal it to players by hand

saveRolls.name: Who rolls saves against traps
saveRolls.hint: Who rolls the die for a character when a trap goes off. The module rolls for characters with no player (except in “The GM decides”).
saveRolls.players: Player clicks a button — the module rolls for them
saveRolls.module: The module rolls, players click nothing
saveRolls.enter: Player rolls their own way and types the result
saveRolls.gm: The GM decides: success or failure

damageMode.name: When trap damage is applied
damageMode.hint: On click: the GM sees in the card who takes how much and presses “Apply”. Right away: damage and conditions apply as soon as the check result is known.
damageMode.button: When the GM clicks “Apply” in the card
damageMode.auto: Automatically, once the result is known

updateCheck.name: Tell me about new versions
updateCheck.hint: When the GM enters the world (at most once an hour), the module asks GitHub whether a new version of Trap Library is out and shows what's new and how to update. Players see nothing.

disarmRolls.name: Who rolls disarm checks
disarmRolls.hint: Player — when the GM clicks the wrench, the character's owner gets a card with a Roll button; the GM's copy has “Roll for the player”. GM — rolled right away. Characters without a player are always rolled by the GM.
disarmRolls.players: The player rolls from a card

playerDisarm.name: Players disarm spotted traps themselves
playerDisarm.hint: A player gets their own wrench next to a trap on the map if they know about it (it's revealed, or the GM told them) and their character stands next to it.
playerDisarm.on: Players have their own wrench on traps they know about
playerDisarm.off: Disarming only through the GM's wrench

Device.title: Device
Device.hint: Describe the trap in-world — damage, DCs and conditions update to match.
Device.controlled: Set by the device: changes when you change its settings.

Editor.title: Configure: {name}
Editor.name: Name
Editor.dragHint: You can drag the card onto the map.
Editor.placeHint: Places it hidden at the center of the view.
Editor.activatorHint: Triggers appear in the trap's area and hit everyone in it. Move them on the map with the teal ✥ handle.
Editor.manualHint: Doesn't fire from footsteps — only from the ▶ button on the map or Set off on the scene tab.

Name.title: Name your trap
Name.label: Name
Name.hint: This is the trap’s name in My traps and on the map.
Name.overHint: This trap was placed from your “{name}”. Update it or save as a new one?

Update.title: Trap Library: version {version} is out
Update.how: To update: on the Foundry setup screen, Add-on Modules → Check for Updates → update Trap Library, then relaunch the world.

Rules.title: Trap Library: trap rules

menu.name: Trap rules
menu.label: Rules
menu.hint: How the module rolls, compares and deals damage in your system: preset, formula, saves, sheet paths, hit points.

Rules.presetHint: Pick a preset — it fills in everything below, then adjust as you like. Save with the button at the bottom.

preset.d20Hint: 1d20 + bonus ≥ DC, half damage on a success, players roll their own saves, damage goes to the token’s HP bar.
preset.gmHint: The module rolls nothing for characters: each target gets Success / Failure buttons. Works in any system, even without a d20.
preset.systemHint: Ready-made rules for {system}: sheet paths, formula and comparison. They also fit similar systems.

Rules.importHint: Paste JSON saved with “Save to file” (yours or someone else’s, for your system).
Rules.imported: Rules loaded — check them and save.
Rules.importBad: This doesn’t look like trap rules (can’t read the JSON).
Rules.saveRollsHint: You can also switch this on the On this scene tab.

fields.formulaHint: @bonus is the character’s bonus. For example: 1d20 + @bonus, 2d6 + @bonus, 1d100.
fields.critDouble: A critical failure on a save and a critical hit deal double damage
fields.askBonus: Ask the player for their bonus when there’s no sheet path
fields.askBonusHint: Otherwise the bonus is 0 (the module rolls a bare die).
fields.acPathHint: For traps with an attack. Empty — the GM marks hit or miss.
fields.typesHint: Comma-separated, in Latin letters: fire, cold, acid… These are labels only — the module doesn’t handle resistances.
fields.disarmFailBy: The trap goes off on a failure by
fields.disarmFailByHint: 0 — a failure never sets it off. With “±10” crits a critical failure sets it off too.

compare.gte: at least the target (d20 + bonus ≥ DC)

targetMode.sheet: A number from the character sheet (OSR saving throw targets)

crits.natural: Highest die face — one step better, a 1 — one step worse
crits.tens: Plus ±10 from the target (four degrees, like PF2e)

Rules.rowsHint: Key — Latin letters (traps refer to it). Bonus path — where the number sits on the sheet: system.abilities.dex.save; add paths with “+” and give a fallback with “|”. Target path — if success means rolling against a number on the sheet (OSR, d100). Own formula and compare — if this check is rolled differently from the rest. Below — which save the catalog traps use to dodge, endure and so on.
Rules.conditionsHint: Which conditions of your system the catalog traps apply. If the system has no such condition, it stays as words in the card.

detect.passive: A passive number from the sheet vs DC
detect.roll: A secret skill check (once per trap)

Rules.probeHint: Select a character token on the scene — I’ll show which numbers the paths find.
Rules.probeEmpty: No paths yet — players will be asked for their bonuses (or it’s 0).
Rules.zeroConfig: You can leave everything as is — traps already work: damage goes to the token’s HP bar and players type in their roll bonus. The settings below just make bonuses come from the character sheet automatically.
Rules.systemKnown: Recognized your system: {system}. Its rules are already filled in — check them and save.
Rules.findHint: Select a character token on the scene and click “Find on sheet” — the module finds where saves, skills, AC and HP live on the sheet and fills in the paths. “Check” shows which numbers are used right now.
Rules.foundTitle: {name}: found {n} paths. Check the numbers and save.
Rules.foundNone: Nothing that looks like saves or skills was found — players will be asked for their bonus. You can type paths by hand in the advanced settings.
Rules.advancedHint: Formula, comparison and crits, your own saves and skills with sheet paths, conditions, noticing. Usually you don’t need to look here.

saveRollsMode.players: The player gets a button in the card. They click it and the module rolls the formula from these rules with the bonus from the sheet (no path — it asks for the bonus); the roll shows in chat.
saveRollsMode.enter: The module rolls nothing. The player rolls their own way — physical dice or their system's sheet with its advantage and bonuses — and types the number into the card.
saveRollsMode.module: The module rolls for everyone right away, quietly; the result goes straight into the card. Players don't click anything.
saveRollsMode.gm: Nobody rolls: the GM gets Success and Failure buttons for each target in the card. Works in any system, even without a d20.

Rules.systemAvailable: Recognized your system: {system}. To fill in its rules, click the “{system}” button below.
